extracted.intended_audience: Users of Magma / computational number theorists performing number field computations
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of Magma functions, conventions and algorithms for creating and manipulating number fields, orders, elements, ideals, subfields, extensions, and computing unit/class groups. Explains expected behavior, representations, and important parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal order in quadratic fields
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quadratic field K = Q(√d), the maximal order MK depends only on d (mod 4): if d ≡ 2,3 (mod 4) then MK = Z[√d], while if d ≡ 1 (mod 4) then MK = Z + Z·(1 + √d)/2. IntegralBasis(K) or Basis(MK) returns [1, epsilond] (the generator for the maximal order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generator may be given an identifier (printname) or printed as epsilond. Example: IntegralBasis(QuadraticField(-3)) returns [1, 1/2*(1 + w)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders and conductor in quadratic fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Every order O of a quadratic field K has a basis [1, f·epsilond], where f (a positive integer) is the conductor (index of O in the maximal order). Conductor(K) returns this index for a given order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suborders of index f can be created with the sub-constructor (e.g., sub< M | 7 > yields the order of conductor 7). The 'generator' for such an order will equal f·epsilond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and coercion of elements in quadratic orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements a ∈ O (order of a quadratic field) can be uniquely written as a0 + a1·f·epsilond with a0,a1 ∈ Z. Eltseq(a) returns the integer coefficient sequence [a0,a1]; coercion from such sequences into O is supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements of an order may be coerced into the field and vice versa; equality tests between order and field elements are performed by lifting to a common overstructure (examples demonstrate matching printed forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis and element representation for general number field orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If O is an order of a degree-n number field K, Basis(O) returns the basis elements (as elements of K); BasisMatrix(O) returns the rational matrix for that basis. Elements of O are represented as integer linear combinations of these basis elements and are printed as coefficient lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eltseq(a) returns the sequence of integer coefficients for a in terms of Basis(O); coercing a coefficient sequence into O creates the element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation order basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis of an equation order E for a number field defined by a polynomial is always the power basis [1, z, z^2, ..., z^{n-1}] where z is a root of the defining polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coercing a field element into the equation order, elements are printed as their coefficient list in that power-basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransformationMatrix(O, P) basis change
rubrics_metrics.description: TransformationMatrix(O, P) returns an n×n integral matrix and a common integer denominator expressing the basis elements of order O as integer linear combinations of the basis of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The matrix (and denominator) can be used to translate coefficient vectors between bases. Use Index(O, E) to get index information between orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRelative(O) for order representation
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRelative(O) returns true if O was constructed via a transformation matrix (i.e., it is not an equation order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flag indicates whether the order's internal representation is relative (given by a transformation) rather than the standard equation-order power-basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: RepresentationMatrix(a) for multiplication action
rubrics_metrics.description: RepresentationMatrix(a) returns the square matrix representing the linear map 'multiply by a'. For field elements the matrix is with respect to the (possibly relative) power basis of the field; for order elements it uses the absolute basis of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matrix can be used to compute products by matrix multiplication on coefficient vectors; examples show RepresentationMatrix for both field and order elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element functions: Norm, Trace, MinimalPolynomial, IsIntegral, IsUnit
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm(a) is the product of conjugates of a (over the ground field). Trace(a) is the sum of conjugates. MinimalPolynomial(a) is the minimal polynomial over the ground field. IsIntegral(a) returns true if a is integral. IsUnit(a) returns true if a is a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions operate on elements of number fields or elements of orders; in relative extensions results are given over the ground field (use AbsoluteNorm/AbsoluteTrace/AbsoluteMinimalPolynomial for Q-based values).

rubrics_metrics.name: NormEquation(O or K, m) search behavior and Exact parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: NormEquation searches for elements of an order O (or the equation order of field K) whose norm equals integer m up to units. If Exact := true is given, the norm must equal m exactly. The function returns a Boolean indicating existence, and if true, a sequence of solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default behavior: norms equal m up to units. The Handbook references additional optional parameters. Example: NormEquation(E,4 : Exact := true) returned false, while NormEquation(E,4) returned true with a solution of norm −4 (equal to 4 up to a unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: AbsoluteNorm/AbsoluteTrace/AbsoluteMinimalPolynomial for absolute computations
rubrics_metrics.description: In relative extensions (FldNum category) Norm/Trace/MinimalPolynomial return values relative to the ground field; use AbsoluteNorm, AbsoluteTrace and AbsoluteMinimalPolynomial to obtain values with respect to Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose absolute vs relative versions depending on whether you want invariants over Q or over the ground field.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComplexConjugate and Conjugate functions in quadratic/cyclotomic fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ComplexConjugate(a) returns the complex conjugate embedding of a for quadratic fields (d<0) and cyclotomic fields; Conjugate(a) for quadratic fields gives the algebraic conjugate. For cyclotomic fields Conjugate(a,k) applies the automorphism ζm ↦ ζm^k (gcd(k,m)=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ComplexConjugate maps chosen embeddings (design choice ζn ↦ e^{2πi/n}, √d ↦ −di for d<0). For cyclotomic fields there can be multiple distinct conjugates corresponding to (Z/mZ)^*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate(a,k) in cyclotomic fields and Galois action
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ∈ Q(ζm), Conjugate(a,k) applies the automorphism sending ζm to ζm^k (k coprime to m), yielding the k-th conjugate. The cyclotomic Galois group is isomorphic to (Z/mZ)^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seqset of conjugates may have fewer elements than the number of automorphisms if some images coincide; examples show enumerating conjugates for z + z^-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of complex embedding for cyclotomic fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma chooses particular complex embeddings for convenience: ζn is sent to e^{2π i/n}, and √d for d<0 is sent to −d·i etc. This determines how cyclotomic and quadratic elements are coerced into ComplexField() numerically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a design choice (customary) and useful when forming explicit real/complex combinations like sin/cos expressed via roots of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: RootOfUnity(n) and RootOfUnity(n, K)
rubrics_metrics.description: RootOfUnity(n) returns a primitive n-th root of unity ζn in Q(ζn). RootOfUnity(n, K) returns ζn inside a given cyclotomic field K = Q(ζm) provided n divides m (or 2m if m is odd).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RootOfUnity to build algebraic expressions for trigonometric values and to combine roots in bigger cyclotomic fields; automatic coercion across cyclotomic fields works via lcm of orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building algebraic sin and cos via roots of unity and finding containing cyclotomic field
rubrics_metrics.description: Define cos(r) and sin(r) via RootOfUnity(r) and combine various roots; Magma will automatically find the smallest cyclotomic field containing the needed roots (the universe will be Q(ζ_L) where L = lcm of required orders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows constructing 3×3 matrices whose entries are cos(2π/3), cos(2π/5), sin(...), and forming MatrixRing(CyclotomicField(60),3) since 60 = lcm(3,5,4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize(a) and MinimalField(a) for cyclotomic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize(~a) mutates a cyclotomic field element a into an element lying in the smallest possible cyclotomic field; Minimize(a) returns such element. MinimalField(a) returns the smallest cyclotomic field containing a (or a set of elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to reduce universe from a larger cyclotomic field to the minimal one (examples reduce from Q(ζ60) to Q(ζ5) or Q(ζ12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic coercion between quadratic and cyclotomic fields and Conductor(K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quadratic field elements contained in a cyclotomic field can be coerced into it, expressing the quadratic element as a sum of roots of unity. The intrinsic function Conductor(K) returns a modulus m such that Q(ζ_m) contains the quadratic field K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for Q(√-13), CyclotomicField(Conductor(Q)) gives Cyclotomic Field of order 52 which contains the quadratic generator expressed in roots of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using MinimalPolynomial to detect subfields containing an element
rubrics_metrics.description: MinimalPolynomial(a) can be used to determine a number field defined by that polynomial which contains the element a; the degree and discriminant of the polynomial reveal the (possible) subfield structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: MinimalPolynomial(ζ7 + ζ7^6) yields x^3 + x^2 − x − 1 (a cubic), detecting that ζ7 + ζ7^6 lies in a cubic subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homomorphisms between cyclotomic and general number fields for coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct homomorphisms h: C -> N between cyclotomic fields and corresponding general number fields (defined by DefiningPolynomial(C)) to coerce elements from cyclotomic fields into subfields of general number fields; then create subfields of N generated by images h(z_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technique allows investigation of whether combinations of roots of unity lie in subfields and to construct those subfields via sub< N | h(z) >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple extensions with NumberField([f1,...,fm])
rubrics_metrics.description: NumberField([f1,f2,...,fm]) creates a tower of (relative) extensions by adjoining roots in the order fm,...,f1; the i-th generator corresponds to the root of fi. Each fi must be irreducible over the previously constructed intermediate field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order of polynomials matters (roots adjoined in sequence). Example: NumberField([x^2-2, x^3-3, x^5-5]) builds a 3-step tower; intermediate fields do not receive explicit names automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: ext constructor for relative extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: ext< K | g > adjoins a root of a monic polynomial g irreducible over K to produce a relative extension of K. This can also be used to extend orders similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma assumes irreducibility over the ground field for efficiency; if g is reducible the result may not be a field (user must ensure irreducibility). Example shows ill-formed extension by x^2-3 over Q(√3) producing a non-field object.

rubrics_metrics.name: GroundField(K), AbsoluteField(L) and AbsoluteOrder
rubrics_metrics.description: GroundField(K) returns the field over which K was defined as an extension; AbsoluteField(L) returns L as an absolute extension (when possible). AbsoluteField only works for simple relative extensions (not for arbitrary multiple extensions). AbsoluteOrder is the analogous function for orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain an absolute description for multiple relative extensions, constructions may have to be repeated or restructured (examples show AbsoluteField usage and errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: sub< K | a >: subfield generated by an element
rubrics_metrics.description: For a relative number field K with ground field G, sub< K | a > returns the relative subfield H = G(a) generated by a single element a ∈ K, together with an embedding H -> K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to isolate the smallest relative field containing a particular element; returns both the field and the embedding map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfields(K) and Subfields(K,m) listing subfields and embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Subfields(K) returns a sequence of pairs <Ki, mi> giving all subfields Ki (except Q) and their embedding homomorphisms mi into K (may include isomorphic repeats). Subfields(K,m) restricts to subfields of degree m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The returned embeddings allow checking equality/isomorphism and mapping primitive elements into K (examples show extracting and using embeddings).

rubrics_metrics.name: BetterPolynomial(K) and BetterPolynomial(K,d) to improve defining polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: BetterPolynomial(K) attempts to find a monic irreducible integer polynomial g defining a number field L isomorphic to K with smaller absolute discriminant than the current defining polynomial. BetterPolynomial(K,d) additionally enforces that a given index divisor d does not divide [OL : EL]. Returns Boolean and (if true) the new field L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used to convert MergeFields output into a field with a 'nicer' defining polynomial (examples show obtaining x^12 − 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: MergeFields(K, L) to produce fields containing both as subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: MergeFields(K,L) returns a sequence of absolute number fields, each containing subfields isomorphic to K and L. Multiple outputs correspond to different choices of embeddings/roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After obtaining candidate merged fields, use BetterPolynomial and Subfields with IsIsomorphic to identify and construct explicit embeddings of K and L into a chosen merged field E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal constructor and basic ideal invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: ideal< O | generators... > constructs ideals in orders O. Invariants and related functions include Index(O,I), Denominator(I), Norm(I), Trace(I), RamificationIndex(p,P), Degree(P), MinimalInteger(I) (least integer contained in ideal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists these invariants; example constructs an ideal and prints its Norm and basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations of ideals: Basis(I), BasisMatrix(I), TransformationMatrix(I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basis(I) returns a Z-basis of the ideal as field elements; BasisMatrix(I) is the rational matrix for this basis; TransformationMatrix(I) returns the transformation matrix (with denominator) for the ideal relative to a basis of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These representations are useful for arithmetic on ideals and converting between presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-element and generator presentations of ideals: Generators, TwoElement, TwoElementNormal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ideal in an order can be generated by at most two elements. Generators(I) returns two generators as order elements, TwoElement(I) returns two field-element generators, and TwoElementNormal returns a normalized two-element presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-element presentations are often cheaper to use once computed (examples show printing TwoElement(I) and Generators(I)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal arithmetic and factorization: multiplication, powering, inversion, Factorization(I), Decomposition(O,p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideals may be multiplied, raised to powers, divided, inverted (yielding fractional ideals with denominators). Factorization(I) returns prime factorization into prime ideals. Decomposition(O,p) gives factorization of pO into prime ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fractional ideals carry an integer denominator; Factorization examples show decomposition into J^2 and recovering J via Factorization(I)[1][1].

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrincipal(I) predicate and generator return
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrincipal(I) returns true and a generator if the (fractional) ideal I is principal, and false otherwise. The test may take significant time in large orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IsPrincipal(J) returned true and provided an explicit generator -n^2 - n + 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other ideal-related functions: Valuation, DegreeOnePrimeIdeals, IsZero/IsIntegral/IsPrime, MultiplicatorRing, pRadical
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuation(I,J) returns valuation of ideal I at prime ideal J. DegreeOnePrimeIdeals(O,b) lists all degree-1 prime ideals in O up to norm b. Predicates IsZero(I), IsIntegral(I), IsPrime(I) indicate zero/integral/prime status. MultiplicatorRing(I) returns the subring of elements multiplying I into itself. pRadical(O,p) returns the ideal of elements with some power in pO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions are used in algorithms such as determining the maximal order and other structural computations; see Table 25.12 for summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class group and unit group functions and their applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions include ClassNumber(K), ClassGroup(K) (and its mapping), ClassGroupStructure(K), UnitGroup(K) (and mapping), TorsionSubgroup(K), UnitRank(K), and Regulator(K). These compute invariants of the ring of integers (maximal order) of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ClassGroup may be applied to an order only if it is known to be maximal. Algorithms for quadratic fields are more efficient; no special optimized algorithms for cyclotomic fields are implemented so one must compute via the corresponding general number field.
